question: does a from-scratch probe-3 re-run of a repaired shard reproduce the repaired shard exactly?

resolution.finding: 2 of 6 re-simulated shards differed from the repaired shards in `qc_flags` only: the stored rows still named step_rheo_1p5x and step_rheo_3p0x protocols that probe-3 does not run for a sample with no usable rheobase
resolution.cause: the repair voided the normalised FEATURE columns but not the QC flags those protocols had raised
resolution.why_no_classification_changes: classify_row reads the SET of flag kinds, not the per-protocol strings; every kind appearing on a normalised protocol also appears on an absolute one in all 15,143 rows, measured with 0 exceptions
resolution.fix: tools/repair_rheobase.py strips step_rheo_*: flags wherever the normalised family is undefined (rheobase NaN or 0). Two bugs in the first attempt at that fix are recorded in the source: QC flags are namespaced with a colon while feature columns use a dot, and the mask must cover rheobase = NaN as well as rheobase = 0
resolution.deterministic_check_added: gate D3 now fails any row carrying a step_rheo_* QC flag while its normalised family is undefined -- checked on all 130,098 rows every run, rather than on a sample of six shards

targeted_reverification.note: the other differing shard (mainen_l5pc) has the same single-row defect from the same cause and costs 2.4 h to re-simulate; the all-rows D3 invariant supersedes it
